The petitioner has filed this claim petition against the respondents U/Sec.166 of M.V.Act for seeking compensation of Rs.25,00,000/ with interest for the death of Shivananjaiah in a Road Traffic Accident took place on 03052020.
2.

The brief contents of the petition are as under:
On 03052020, at about 08.30 a.m., the deceased was proceeding on his motorcycle bearing reg.No.KA44 S4331 along with petitioner no.1 and when they reached near Mavinakere - Mayasandra Main Road, at that time, the rider of the Bajaj Pulsar Motorcycle bearing reg.No.KA16EM1920 ridden the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the deceased motorcycle.
Due to which the deceased succumbed to the injuries on the spot.

Thereafter the dead body was SCCH-10 shifted to Government hospital, Turuvekere for postmortem and the postmortem was conducted the dead body was handed over to the petitioners and they have performed funeral and obsequious ceremony.
Further the petitioner no.1 is the wife, petitioner No.2 and 3 are the son and daughter of the deceased and they are the legal heirs of deceased Shivananjaiah.
Further at the time of accident, the deceased was hale and healthy and aged about 62 years, working as an Agriculturist and milk vendor and earning Rs.25,000/ p.m.
Hence the petitioners prays to award compensation of Rs.25,00,000/ from the respondents under all heads together with interest and costs.

The petitioners have filed this petition claiming compensation of Rs.25,00,000/ with respect to the death of Shivananjaiah in the road traffic accident.

To prove the accident and the accident was occurred due to the sole negligence on the part of the rider of the offending motorcycle bearing reg.

The Ex.P.1 is the FIR, Ex.P.2 is the complaint, Ex.P.3 is the spot mahazar, Ex.P.4 is the IMV report, Ex.P.5 is the inquest panchanama, Ex.P.6 is the PM report,

12. The respondent No.1 and 2 have disputed the accident as the accident was not occurred on the SCCH-10 negligence of rider of the offending motorcycle.

The respondent No.1 contended that, the deceased has ridden the motorcycle bearing reg.No.KA44S4331 in rash and negligent manner and without observing the vehicles on main road, thereby he dashed his motorcycle to the offending motorcycle and caused the accident.
13. To prove the defence, the official of the respondent No.1 company got examined as RW1 and produced the documents as Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.9.

After the accident the case was registered against the rider of the offending motorcycle bearing reg.No.KA16EM 1920 and the police have investigated the matter and filed charge sheet against the rider of the offending motorcycle for the offence punishable under section 279, 338, 304(A) of IPC and Sec.181 of M.V.Act.
The petitioner also produced the spot mahazar, IMV report, inquest panchanama and PM report and charge sheet as per Ex.P.3 to 7.

Though the respondent No.1/insurance SCCH-10 company contended that, there is no negligence on the part of the rider of the offending motorcycle, but no material is produced before the court to substantiate their contention except to show the police have filed the charge sheet for the offence punishable U/Sec.181 of M.V.Act as the rider of the offending motorcycle had violated the Sec.3 and 4 of M.V.Act as there is no DL to the rider of the offending motorcycle.
14. Though the respondent no.1 has cross examined the PW1, but nothing has been elicited from the mouth of the petitioner No.1/Pw1 to show the accident was occurred on the negligence of the deceased.

Therefore in view of the oral and documentary evidence produced by the petitioners, I am of the opinion that, the accident was occurred on sole negligence of the rider of the offending motorcycle bearing reg.No.KA16EM1920.
In the said accident the deceased died on spot.

Hence,
I answer the issue No.1 and 2 are in the affirmative.

16. ISSUE No.4:
In this case, the respondents have disputed the accident as it was not occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending SCCH-10 motor cycle.
On the contrary the accident was occurred due to the negligence of deceased.
Further the respondent No.1 contended that, the rider of the offending motorcycle had not valid and driving license.
In this case, the respondent No.1 has examined the Assistant Manager of respondent no.1 company as Rw1 and produced the documents as per Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.9.

The Ex.R.1 is the authorization letter, Ex.R.2 is the policy copy, Ex.R.3 is the copy of notice, Ex.R.4 is the postal receipt, Ex.P.5 is the postal acknowledgement, Ex.R.6 is the notice u/s.133 of M.V.Act issued by the police to the owner of offending vehicle, Ex.R.7 is the copy of reply notice issued by the owner, Ex.R.8 is the copy notice u/s.133 of M.V.Act to the owner of the motorcycle bearing reg.No.KA44S4331 and Ex.R.9 is the reply.

On perusal of the Ex.R.6 and Ex.R.8 i.e., reply notice issued by the owners of the motorcycle to the SCCH-10 notice U/s.133 have stated that the rider of the offending motorcycle and the rider of the motorcycle bearing reg.No.KA44S4331 have not Driving license at the time of accident.

The petitioners have relied the decision reported in 2019 ACJ 42 between Saraswathi Palariya and others V/s. New Indian Assurance Co.Ltd., and others, wherein it was held that: "Negligence - Contributory negligence - Driving License - High Court fixed contributory negligence on the deceased on the ground that deceased was driving the vehicle without a driving licence - Held :
driving without a driving licence may expose the person to other liabilities but no inference of contributory negligence can be drawn on that basis.

sentences.text: In this decision, the Hon'ble Apex court clearly held that though the deceased had not Driving License itself is not a ground to inference contributory negligence.
SCCH-10
Therefore in this case the respondents have not placed any material to show there is a contributory negligence of the deceased in the accident except he has not Driving License.

The nonhaving DL itself is not a ground to contributory negligence,
unless proved the contributory negligence.
In this case the respondents have not proved the contributory negligence of the deceased.
The documents produced by the petitioners, it clearly established that, the deceased died due to the accident on the negligence of the rider of the offending motorcycle.
Therefore the petitioners are entitled for the compensation.

In a recent decision in National Insurance Company Limited v. Birender [(2020) 11 SCC 356], a claim petition filed by major married and earning sons of the deceased mother, the Honourable Supreme Court held as follows:
"12.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited v. Birender [(2020) 11 SCC 356]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The legal representatives of the deceased could move application for compensation by virtue of clause (c) of Section 166 (1).
The major married son who is also earning and not fully dependent on the deceased would be still covered by the expression "legal representative" of the deceased.

This Court in Manjuri Bera (supra)
had expounded that liability to pay compensation under the Act does not cease because of absence of dependency of the concerned legal representative.
Notably, the expression "legal representative" has not SCCH-10 been defined in the Act.
xxx xxx xxxx 13.

In paragraph 15 of the said decision, while adverting to the provisions of Section 140 of the Act,
the Court observed that even if there is no loss of dependency, the claimant, if he was a legal representative, will be entitled to compensation.

In the concurring judgment of Justice S.H.
Kapadia, as His Lordship then was, it is observed that there is distinction between "right to apply for compensation" and "entitlement to compensation".
The compensation constitutes part of the estate of the deceased.
As a result, the legal representative of the deceased would inherit the estate.

Indeed,
in that case, the Court was dealing with the case of a married daughter of the deceased and the efficacy of Section 140 of the Act.
Nevertheless, the principle underlying the exposition in this decision would clearly and 2 (claimants) even though they are major sons of the deceased and also earning.
14. It is thus settled by now that the legal representatives of the deceased have a right to apply for compensation.

Having SCCH-10 said that, it must necessarily follow that even the major married and earning sons of the deceased being legal representatives have a right to apply for compensation and it would be the bounden duty of the Tribunal to consider the application irrespective of the fact whether the concerned legal representative was fully dependant on the deceased and not to limit the claim towards conventional heads only.

The evidence on record in the present case would suggest that the claimants were working as agricultural labourers on contract basis and were earning meagre income between Rs. 1,00,000/and Rs. 1,50,000/per annum.
In that sense, they were largely dependant on the earning of their mother and in fact, were staying with her, who met with an accident at the young age of 48 years."

50. It is trite that the Courts in construing a social welfare legislation has to adopt a beneficial rule of construction which would fulfil the policy of the legislation favourable to those in whose interest the enactment has been passed.

51. It would be preposterous to accept the contention of the learned counsel for the appellant that a 25 year old daughter would be no longer dependent on her 49 year old mother because she was given in marriage.
The bond between a mother and a daughter is eternal.
I reminisce the quotation of Cardinal Mermillod  "No matter how old she may be, sometimes a girl just needs her mom."
The Hon'ble Kerala High Court has considered the judgment of the Apex Court in the above decision.

Therefore, in view of the principle laid down by the Hon'ble High Court of Kerala and Hon'ble Supreme Court, which is referred in the above decision, I am of SCCH-10 the opinion that,
the married daughter and major son are also dependents to the deceased and they are entitled for the compensation under the motor vehicle accident cases.

On perusal of the contents of petition and contents of objection statement, it reveals that, the respondent No.1 is the insurer and the respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending motorcycle.

Further, as stated above that, the alleged accident has occurred due to rash and negligent riding of SCCH-10 the rider of the offending motorcycle bearing reg.No.KA 16EM1920 and the policy was in force as on the date of accident.

The respondent No.1 contended that, the police have filed the charge sheet against the rider of the offending motorcycle bearing reg.No.KA16EM1920 for offence punishable under section 279, 338, 304(A) of IPC and Sec.181 of M.V.Act as the rider of the motorcycle had not driving license at the time of accident.
The respondent No.1 contended that, the rider of the offending motorcycle had not driving license, therefore there is a breach of policy conditions.
Therefore the insurance company is not liable to pay the compensation.
28. To support of it the insurance company has lead the evidence of its official as RW1 and produced the documents as Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.8.

The Ex.R.1 is the authorization letter, Ex.R.2 is the policy copy, Ex.R.3 is SCCH-10 the copy of notice, Ex.R.4 is the postal receipt, Ex.P.5 is the postal acknowledgement, Ex.R.6 is the notice u/s.133 of M.V.Act issued by the police to the owner of offending vehicle, Ex.R.7 is the copy of reply notice issued by the owner, Ex.R.8 is the copy notice u/s.133 of M.V.Act to the owner of the motorcycle bearing reg.No.KA44S4331 and Ex.R.9 is the reply.

The Ex.R.7 is the reply issued by the owner of the offending motorcycle, clearly stated that the rider of the offending motorcycle had not driving license at the time of accident.

The counsel for the petitioners argued that, though the rider of the motorcycle has not Driving license, but the policy was in force, therefore the insurance company is liable to pay the compensation as they had indemnify to the insured and relied the decisions reported in AIR 2018 SC 592 between Pappu SCCH-10 and others V/s. sentences.text: In the above decision and discussions, the Hon'ble Apex Court held that, where the driver did not possess a driving license and there is a breach of policy conditions.
In this case the petitioner is the third party claimant.

Therefore in view of violation of policy conditions, the liability has to be sladded on owner of the vehicle, but in view of the policy to the motorcycle by respondent No.2 though rider of the motorcycle had not valid effective driving licence, at the time of accident, but in view of policy and indemnify of the insurer to the owner, the insurer is liable to pay the compensation to the third party injured and insurer has right to recover the same from the owner as a deceased is a third party.

However, the respondent No.1 being the insurer of alleged motorcycle is liable to pay compensation of Rs.9,62,028/ with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit and recover the same SCCH-10 from the owner/respondent No.2.
Accordingly, I answer the issue No.4 in the partly affirmative.

Further contended that, at the time of accident the rider of the alleged motorcycle was not having valid and effective driving license to ridden the motorcycle and the respondent No.2 has violated terms and conditions of the policy.
Further the respondent SCCH-10 no.1 contended that, the deceased was riding the motorcycle in rash and negligent manner without having valid and effective driving licence and dashed to the pulser motorcycle and caused the accident.

The petitioners have filed this petition claiming compensation of Rs.25,00,000/ with respect to the death of Shivananjaiah in the road traffic accident.
opennyai_summary.issue:
3 ISSUES 1.
Whether the petitioners prove that on 03 052020 at about 8.30 p.m. the deceased by name Shivananjaiah was proceeding on a motorcycle bearing reg.No.KA44S 4331 and when he reached near Mavinakere Mayasandra Main Road, at that time, the rider of the Bajaj Pulsar Motorcycle bearing reg.No.KA16 EM1920 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the deceased motorcycle, as a result, he sustained injury and succumbed to the said injury and died on the spot?
2. Whether the petitioners prove that the accident has mainly occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending Bajaj Pulsar Motorcycle?
3. Whether the petitioners prove that they are the only legal heirs and the dependents of the deceased?
4. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation as prayed? if so, at what rate and from whom?
5. What order or award?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
After the accident the case was registered against the rider of the offending motorcycle bearing reg.No.KA16EM 1920 and the police have investigated the matter and filed charge sheet against the rider of the offending motorcycle for the offence punishable under section 279, 338, 304(A) of IPC and Sec.181 of M.V.Act.
Though the respondent No.1/insurance SCCH-10 company contended that, there is no negligence on the part of the rider of the offending motorcycle, but no material is produced before the court to substantiate their contention except to show the police have filed the charge sheet for the offence punishable U/Sec.181 of M.V.Act as the rider of the offending motorcycle had violated the Sec.3 and 4 of M.V.Act as there is no DL to the rider of the offending motorcycle.
In this case the petitioners are the wife and children of deceased and claiming compensation of Rs.25,00,000/.
To prove the said fact, the petitioner No.1 got examined as PW1 and produced documents.
To prove the income of the deceased, the petitioners have not produced any documents to show that the deceased was doing milk vending business and agriculture and earning of Rs.25,000/p.m.
In the absence of documentary evidence the notional income of the deceased has to be taken into consideration.
The accident was occurred on 03.05.2020.
19. As per the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court reported in 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC) (National Insurance Company Limited Vs Pranay Sethi and others), if the person died in the motor accident, the income with respect to the future prospect has to taken into consideration while awarding compensation.
The Hon'ble Apex court has not permitted to take the future prospects for the income of the deceased aged above 60 years at the time of accident.
In this case, the date of year of the deceased as per Ex.P.9 is 1957 and the accident took place on 03.05.2020, as on the date of accident the deceased aged about 63 years.
Therefore it is not permissible to award the compensation by including the future prospects.
Hence, the future prospects is not taken into consideration.
Smt.Maniyamma vs The Oriental Insurance Co.Ltd on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159176787/
8 20.
The deceased died living behind three dependents.
23. Further, as Law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others, the compensation towards loss t o estate, funeral expenses is to be awarded.
In view of decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the New India Assurance Co.Ltd. V/s. Smt.
Somwati and others in Civil Appeal No.3093/2020 with other Civil appeals decided on 0709 2020, wherein Hon'ble Apex Court held that, in view of death of a parents, the children are entitled compensation under the head of Love and Affection.
In view of the sudden death of the father, the petitioner No.2 and 3 have lost their love and affection towards the deceased.
Therefore it has to be compensated as a just compensation.
The respondent No.1 contended that, the rider of the offending motorcycle had not driving license, therefore there is a breach of policy conditions.
Therefore the insurance company is not liable to pay the compensation.
Smt.Maniyamma vs The Oriental Insurance Co.Ltd on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159176787/
10
Therefore in view of violation of policy conditions, the liability has to be sladded on owner of the vehicle, but in view of the policy to the motorcycle by respondent No.2 though rider of the motorcycle had not valid effective driving licence, at the time of accident, but in view of policy and indemnify of the insurer to the owner, the insurer is liable to pay the compensation to the third party injured and insurer has right to recover the same from the owner as a deceased is a third party.
